title: D. Fixing a Binary String

Reverse the substring s1s2…sps1s2…sps_1 s_2 \ldots s_p. After this step, the string s1s2…sns1s2…sns_1 s_2 \ldots s_n will become spsp−1…s1sp+1sp+2…snspsp−1…s1sp+1sp+2…sns_p s_{p-1} \ldots s_1 s_{p+1} s_{p+2} \ldots s_n.  Then, perform a cyclic shift of the string sss to the left ppp times. After this step, the initial string s1s2…sns1s2…sns_1s_2 \ldots s_n will become sp+1sp+2…snspsp−1…s1sp+1sp+2…snspsp−1…s1s_{p+1}s_{p+2} \ldots s_n s_p s_{p-1} \ldots s_1. For example, if you apply the operation to the string 110001100110 with p=3p=3p=3, after the second step, the string will become 011001100110, and after the third step, it will become 001100110011.A string sss is called kkk-proper if two conditions are met:  s1=s2=…=sks1=s2=…=sks_1=s_2=\ldots=s_k;  si+k≠sisi+k≠sis_{i+k} \neq s_i for any iii (1≤i≤n−k1≤i≤n−k1 \le i \le n - k). For example, with k=3k=3k=3, the strings 000, 111000111, and 111000 are kkk-proper, while the strings 000000, 001100, and 1110000 are not.You are given an integer kkk, which is a divisor of nnn. Find an integer ppp (1≤p≤n1≤p≤n1 \le p \le n) such that after performing the operation, the string sss becomes kkk-proper, or determine that it is impossible. Note that if the string is initially kkk-proper, you still need to apply exactly one operation to it.
inputSpecification:
Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains one integer ttt (1≤t≤1041≤t≤1041 \le t \le 10^4) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains two integers nnn and kkk (1≤k≤n1≤k≤n1 \le k \le n, 2≤n≤1052≤n≤1052 \le n \le 10^5) — the length of the string sss and the value of kkk. It is guaranteed that kkk is a divisor of nnn.
The second line of each test case contains a binary string sss of length nnn, consisting of the characters 0 and 1.

title: C. Zero Path
